items.note: S2.3.4b-d and S2.3.5 follow the proof: the net change (JV+RG)x does not depend on the scratch values, the intersection coefficients cancel, and the three stages give (-y,x). The neighbour counts and wire-count formulas (767-782) are not given, and neither is h=100; S2.3.6 says only that W is fixed.
The invariant proof (definition at sources, edge operator, linearity at gates) and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} are reproduced as in the paper.

The plan reproduces the forms, the stage transitions, the gate-label table, the residual table, the telescoping to Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, and the F_2 orthonormal-basis argument. The symbols a=h^{j-1} and f=h^{3-j} in the residual table are left undefined, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539 are quoted rather than computed, as they are in the paper.

The projection assignment, rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N exceptional 2P_{U_a} source edges, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m, and the endpoint identity P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m all follow the proof; S2.9.6 turns the identity into the shear H<-H+D.

Weight additivity mod 4, odd weight of norm-one vectors giving one kernel aI+bX_v per basis vector, the count s_c, the k-column tensoring, the weight-27 pair repaired by Z conjugation, and the final negation and routing are all reproduced in the paper's order.

L/N<1/2 gives deficits N-2L_b and 2N-2L_c, and the plan gives the exact eta_b and eta_c (above 20*2^{-50}), log m<20 and m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-eta), hence s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. The eta values are quoted, not computed, matching the paper.

The elementary operations (by the split/scan/merge method), the cyclic row split and the controlled shift (split at Q-a, merge reversed, offset work absorbed) are derived. The plan's statement and derivation omit the multiplication by fixed rational units and negation of Lemma ordered-affine-streams (592-614), which S2.8.5 later relies on.

The elimination order, the triangular updates in descending order, the E_2/E_1^{-1} sequence and the three-update single interchange give exactly a interchanges, as in the paper. The choice of an odd prime that avoids denominators and diagonal numerators (1413-1423) is missing from S2.8; S2.5.6b and S2.9.2 imply it.

The proof is followed step by step: role streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} by recursive interchanges, the frame identity giving Phi_{I_m}, the merge, the three updates, s calls, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) solved in both cases, and the fixed-tape schedule with descriptor bounds.

The plan follows the paper: the high-digit row field with R=q^{2rho}>=W^k, padding to a multiple of W^k, base-m pieces summing to O(Ve^tau), unpadding, the binary-to-radix-q padding, and the case of widths that differ by one bit.

The plan follows the paper: P_M conjugation that needs only invertibility, the slot/column layout, one forward child per basis vector (the inverse via (C^{-1})^{(x)f}=(-i)^f Z C Z), at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, s_c children of e/m axes, and H_0^{(x)D}=b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D.

The plan follows the paper: the eight conditional additions with their parity cycles, the guard values, the packed cyclic shifts, the bad set with the union bound delta_bad, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting B, radix-sort repair, the top position, the cost terms and the application to row additions.

The plan derives the node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), the rows from the first q_0 chunks padded to W^{k_0}, children of V/W, the recurrence with leaves O(e), the internal and leaf sums, and the base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}), as in the paper.

The plan follows the paper: the guard width with E, B, nu=11, C_1=20, the depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, Delta=o(p), the proof's uniform packed-call bounds, and one final truncation with error below sqrt2*2^{-p}.

The plan derives character cancellation without division, DIF in bit-reversed order with the reverse procedure, grouped rounds, the layout (prefix moves, Dq-1 chunk exchanges), the per-round layer calls, one truncation per round and LBF^- / F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, all as in the paper. S3.9 misstates the per-round cost of prefix rounds (see errors).

The plan follows the proof: evaluation at B_0=2^{4p} with signed carries, four products, the |h_j|<B_0/2 separation, centered extraction with its residual identity, negacyclic wrap, truncation, and the O(rp log(rp)) total.
The plan follows the paper: the retained LB order with P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v), the normalization identity, the error 2delta+eta then 3delta+eta scaled by M, the output width and the cost.

The plan follows the paper: the Gaussian maps, N=CTD, the Neumann inverse, the power-of-two normalizations giving 2^{2alpha^2}, the selector C, the quoted error and time table, the removal of the two sorts, and the tensor form on the padded box with axis exposure O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)).

Periodicity of the chirp and the coefficient conj(a_j)a_{j-k}conj(a_k)/T give the permuted Bluestein identity. Dilation by units gives RF^+R=F^+, and the convolution rule gives (u*v)/S^2, as in the proof.

The plan derives the fixed rationals and their checks, the sizes and comparison constants, alpha, gamma, eta, and the prime-interval count. It also covers the disjoint intervals, T/2<S<T by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i>p, the n^{o(1)} search and the no-wraparound capacity bound, as in the paper.
The isomorphism argument, the triangular formula b_i=a_i+mu_i sum_{j<i} a_j P_j, the update order, the padded bijection, the prefix-controlled shifts and the O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)) cost follow the paper.

The plan follows the paper: well-definedness, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, identical formats, the computed twist sequence and its error below 6TL h_p.

The plan gives the chirp transform, the source transform with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A=RF_s, the conjugated opposite procedure, the six steps, and the explanation of the two scalings by S, all as in the paper.

The plan carries the error chain E_ring<5TL, the chirp error below 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL and E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L, with the disk margins. It then shows the final error below 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, the rounding, and carry propagation with its invariant, as in the paper.

The plan derives the cost table rows, the margins g_1..g_7 with minimum 2^{-181}=2kappa, the o(Tp) setup and exceptional-sort charges, absorption of log factors by p^kappa, and the schoolbook cutoff, as in the paper.

S0 asserts that the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model, and S1.1 recalls the conjecture. No step states what an eventual lower bound means or that O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) gives liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0.

errors.says: The rounds on prefix slots cost O(Tp) per round and O(TpdK) in total.
errors.paper: Each participating bit is processed individually, and its moves and scans cost O(Tp). A round with up to D<=d bits therefore costs O(TpD), and at most b+1<=K rounds give O(TpdK). An O(Tp) per-round cost would not yield the stated total.

errors.says: Method: prescribe terminal labels U_a, 0 and the full space on the data and scratch roles.
errors.paper: The sink label of Y_a is U_a^perp, of dimension m-1. This label makes the sink dimensions sum to Wm-N. With only U_a, 0 and F as terminal labels, the sinks would sum to Wm.

chain: The tree reaches O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) by the paper's route. S2 builds both power-saving tape procedures from the rank-saving networks (frames, labels, s<Wm, the E_1 Pi E_2 shear count, row-split recurrences, packed bit additions). S3-S4 give synthetic transforms and ring convolution, S5 gives resampling with retained permutations, chirps and cancellation, and S6 gives the parameters, CRT map, twist, six-step algorithm, exact recovery and cost table. The plan is thin in four places: it never states the network sizes (h=100, N, m=h^3, I, c, the wire counts W); it quotes L/N and eta exactly as the paper does without computing them; it omits the rational-unit scalings of the controlled-shift lemma; and it asserts the disproof of the conjecture without the liminf argument.

steps.note: The exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with every scratch wire restored is fully derived. The plan never states h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 or m=h^3, and it never says the data are indexed by a in T^3 (only u_a=t_{a1}(x)t_{a2}(x)t_{a3} appears). So the defining sizes are missing, and the conservative verdict is mentioned.
A common invertible frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. Each edge applies only D_v D_u^{-1}, and the intermediate frames are free.
The plan gives nondegenerate labels in F^{(x)3} of dimension m and comparable labels on every edge. The only decreasing edges are the central edges from time 3 to 4, each losing h.
rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, so each edge costs its label dimension change. The N first edges on X_a have matrix 2P_{U_a} of rank one with zero dimension change.
The plan has sum|Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b once the N source ranks are added.
L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 are both below 1/2. This gives the deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0, hence s<Wm.
M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m on every role (P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m on X_a, 0 and I elsewhere). Through Phi_M frames this gives H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included.
A rank-a shear factors as E_1 Pi E_2 and costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V), so a node makes exactly s recursive calls, each on a stream of volume V/W.
The plan has F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20, giving F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: 8 of 9 steps reconstructed. The plan carries frames, labels with central-only losses, rank equal to dimension change with the N source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L and s_b, L/N<1/2, the endpoint identity giving the shear, the E_1 Pi E_2 count of s recursive calls, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. Only C1 falls short: the network's exchange-and-restore mechanism is derived, but its sizes h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never stated.
